payload.instruction: Stuffing the paper into the cup
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Given the inventory and nested boundary map, does independent inspection establish completed stuffing, affirmative incompleteness, or unresolved completion, and what requested progress is actually established?
node.criteria: Pass only when established paper-and-cup identity and concrete entry, containment, or compression establish completed stuffing; some paper may remain outside. Fail when affirmative geometry establishes incomplete insertion, wholly external placement, rim-only placement without stuffing, or adequately visible absence of a required object. Report whether this failure accompanies positive requested insertion progress or established no progress. Unknown when completion requires an unresolved spatial relation or receiver identity, or when established entry cannot be distinguished as intermediate versus completed stuffing. A boundary-mapping pass is not positive entry evidence. Unresolved source correspondence alone does not invalidate established spatial evidence, but an unresolved edited receiver identity prevents claiming insertion into a cup.
node.binding: Consume s1 and s4_opening_entry in saved order as context, then inspect the edited image independently. Read the nested check's typed identity, geometry, progress, and completion findings rather than treating its execution status as their truth value. Revisit specifically localized hidden paper segments and test whether visible containment, compression, or boundary continuity settles stuffing extent. Resolve conflicts only with explicit visible evidence. Do not promote a mapping pass to entry, an entry finding to completion, or completion failure to no progress. Preserve genuine hidden-entry uncertainty; do not infer missing visual facts from the instruction, source cup, hand grip, or altered printing.

dependencies.evidence: Source: a large white sheet of paper is visible at left, beside a blue cup lying on its side at right; the cup has a broad oval rim/opening and tapered enclosing walls. Edited: a blue printed paper/card is clearly visible, held by a hand, with its boundaries mostly discernible. Behind it is a reddish rounded object with a dark curved line, but the paper and framing obscure much of its contour; the visible structure does not establish that it is a cup. Direct comparison therefore does not establish whether the source cup corresponds to the edited receiving object. The images allow a grounded inventory, while edited cup identity and source-to-edit correspondence remain unresolved.

Boundary map: the blue printed paper/card has a visible upper edge running from the hand-held upper-left area toward a pointed upper-right corner; its right edge descends along the reddish rounded object, and its lower edge angles back to a lower-left corner. The hand occludes parts of the paper’s left/upper boundary; the visible paper edges and corners otherwise define its outline. The reddish object is visible to the right and below the paper, with a dark curved line across it; the paper overlaps its left portion in the image, but no visible boundary establishes a cup opening or paper passing behind a rim. No other plausible receiver is evident. Findings: receiver identity unresolved; geometry unresolved (neither entry nor wholly external placement is established); requested progress unresolved; completion unresolved. The visible overlap and obscured contact area do not determine whether paper enters a cup.
